description: We are Team Glitch, building ArtemisLens—an AI-powered 3D lunar south pole mission simulator for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. Using real NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data and LRO elevation maps, our platform visualizes dynamic sun shadows, calculates solar power windows, and verifies Earth communication line-of-sight in real time. Looking for teammates in 3D web dev (Three.js/React), Python data pipelines, astrophysics, and storytelling to build a global-finalist prototype!
summary: ArtemisLens is an interactive lunar mission planning platform and 6-DOF physics-true landing simulator engineered for the Artemis program's targeted south polar landing sites (85°S–90°S). Powered by NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) LOLA elevation models and NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris vectors, ArtemisLens models the complete 708-hour lunar synodic cycle. It calculates continuous solar power availability on the "Peaks of Eternal Light," evaluates Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication locks through complex lunar libration, and provides multi-site trade evaluations across candidate landing zones like Shackleton Ridge and Malapert Massif. Furthermore, it features a playable 120 Hz flight simulator implementing authentic Apollo-style guidance algorithms (P63 Braking, P64 Approach, P66 Terminal Descent) with realistic throttle lag and speed-of-light comms delay. ArtemisLens operates with complete fidelity both online and 100% offline, serving as a dual-purpose tool for mission trajectory analysis and next-generation STEM aerospace education.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

ArtemisLens addresses the critical challenges of surface solar power planning and precision landing at the lunar south pole (85°S–90°S):

- Horizon Ray-Casting & Solar Modeling: Ingests high-resolution LRO LOLA Digital Elevation Models (DEM) over 128x128 elevation grids (250 m/pixel) centered on high-priority Artemis candidates. It computes 360-degree topocentric horizon occlusion masks to simulate the full 708-hour lunar synodic day/night cycle, calculating solar illumination, thermal eclipse intervals, and solar array electrical yield (1361 W/m² solar constant, 30% triple-junction photovoltaic efficiency).

- Direct-to-Earth (DTE) Comms Libration: Uses NASA JPL Horizons topocentric vectors to track Earth’s oscillation relative to local terrain rims, forecasting communication blackout windows.

- Physics-True 6-DOF Powered Descent: Runs a 120 Hz numerical integration engine incorporating lunar gravity (1.62 m/s²), variable propellant mass flow (Isp = 311–380 s), engine throttle response lag (tau = 0.12 s), and Apollo PGNCS guidance logic (P63 Braking, P64 Approach, P66 Terminal Descent).

- Dual-Persona Mission Copilot: Features real-time telemetry assessment through a Flight Director mode (operational GO/NO-GO landing recommendations) and a Mission Educator mode (accessible orbital mechanics explanations).

2. What benefits and intended impact does it have?

- Operational Feasibility: Enables mission designers to identify optimal landing sites and solar outpost locations based on multi-variable trade studies (illumination percentage, slope stability, and continuous eclipse risk).

- STEM Engagement: Brings complex orbital mechanics and Apollo guidance algorithms to students and the public through an intuitive, interactive 3D WebGL interface.

- 100% Offline Resilience: Employs an offline mathematical orbital model so field teams and classrooms can run full mission simulations without internet access.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, and Technologies Used

- Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Framer Motion, Zustand, Recharts, Tailwind CSS.

- Backend: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn, NumPy.

- Scientific Models: NASA JPL Horizons Ephemeris API, LRO LOLA DEM datasets, Meeus astronomical algorithms.

4. Creativity and Considerations

- Unified a scientific solar exposure calculator with a playable Apollo-era 6-DOF guidance simulation.

- Modeled authentic operational constraints often omitted in simulators: 2.6-second speed-of-light comms delay buffer, particulate dust storm blowout during landing, and lunar night floodlight operations.
